question.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc$, $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,4,3⟩$, $c=⟨2,-6,-4⟩$, and  $u=⟨3,-7,-4⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
question.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -6 \\ -4\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+2t=3 \\ 4s-6t=-7 \\ 3s-4t=-4\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 \\ 4 & -6 & -7 \\ 3 & -4 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5 \\ 3 & -4 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}-s+2t=3 \\ 2t=5 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
2t=5\,⟹\,t=\frac{5}{2}.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s+2t & =3 \\ -s+2(\frac{5}{2}) & =3 \\ -s+5 & =3 \\ -s & =-2 \\ s & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=2,\,t=\frac{5}{2},$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=2b+\frac{5}{2}c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=2\cdot \frac{5}{2}=5.$
